newsitem.title: USA: Control board chief lauds $168.8 mln DC bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Control board chief lauds $168.8 mln DC bond sale.

text.p: The chairman of the District of Columbia financial control board said on Thursday that today's sale of $168.8 million in general obligation bonds "marks the return of the District to the capital markets."
"Today's sale represents a vote of confidence in the District by the financial markets," said Andrew Brimmer, in a press statement.

Brimmer added, however, "there remains much to be done. The District has made a good beginning in its recovery, but continuing cooperation among the Mayor, CFO, City Council and the Authority are necessary."
Also today, a key Merrill Lynch & Co. analyst said one of the keys to today's successful sale by the District of Columbia of $168.8 million in GOs was improved financial disclosure by the city.

"There were dry spells of information over the years (and) that drought contributed to widening spreads" in the sale of D.C. bonds, said John Hallacy, managing director of municipal bond research at Merrill, said at a meeting of bond analysts here.

Hallacy, whose firm headed today's winning syndicate, said D.C. has become more forthcoming, including its release on Oct. 1 of a supplement to a Sept. 18 preliminary official statement for the GO bonds.
"Today's sale is watershed event in terms of being a predicter of what happens in the future," Hallacy said.

Hallacy said spreads on D.C. 20-year GOs have been narrowing when compared to New York City 20-year GOs. "The levels today indicated that DC (stands) at 650 and the equivalent New York City (GOs) would be about 630," he said.
"That's probably the narrowest spread we've had in some time," Hallacy said.
